text.p: Poland's furniture maker Swarzedzkie Fabryki Mebli Swarzedz SA, which had a net loss of 6.7 million zlotys in the first six months of 1996, plans a debt-for-equity scheme, the spokesman of the company said.

Sebastian Szesny told Reuters the firm wanted to issue shares or convertible bonds early next year. He said some of them would be taken by the firm's creditors and some by a strategic investor which the company was looking for.

"We're planning a new share issue or convertible bonds issue. At least a part of them could be taken by the firm's creditors and a part, possibly, by a strategic investor," he said, but declined to give details.
He did not reveal the extent of the debts.
Szczesny said the plan had already been accepted by the supervisory board of the company but had yet to be approved by the general shareholders meeting, due later in the year.
He said the firm already signed an agreement with consortium of Polish Development Bank (PBR) and law firm KNS on preparing the issue, offering and underwriting the shares or bonds.
Late in July Swarzedz signed an agreement with its main creditors suspending debt payments for three months.
